rules.expected: Actual calculations support an alkene-associated triplet/open-shell excited state of this substrate whose energy is compatible with TXO sensitization conditions and which can serve as the reactive starting point for skeletal rearrangement. Compare compatible excitation-energy definitions, electronic states and solvents. The paper's 52.2 is a Gibbs energy difference between states, not a vertical electronic excitation energy; TXO 65.5 is a literature reference, not an actual calculation from this verification. Neither number has a scoring tolerance. The lamp wavelength alone or repetition of the authors' mechanism does not earn credit. An additional calculation of the carbonyl triplet at 75.6 to exclude a Norrish pathway is not required.

rules.expected: For cis/trans comparisons with the same target-product connectivity graph, the same conditions and compatible physical quantities, calculations support a lower free energy for the cis product, with the C1 methoxycarbonyl and C7 phenyl groups on the same face, than for trans. The two relative configurations must actually be distinguished; do not infer the result backward from the known cis observation. The paper's 23.5 is a Gibbs energy difference, whereas the approximately 3.7 difference at the crossing points is an electronic energy difference; they must not be mixed. Crossing points may provide additional relevant evidence, but a new MECP trajectory or crossing-point numerical threshold is not mandatory. The product stability difference itself is neither a room-temperature isomerization rate nor a precise dr.

rules.expected: Finally, explicitly connect the calculated preference for cis over trans in this system to the observed same-face relationship of the C1 methoxycarbonyl/C7 phenyl groups, providing a bounded energetic/structural explanation. Distinguish the thermodynamic product preference from possible selectivity factors involving ring closure/crossing. Merely stating that cis is more stable without applying the evidence to the given stereochemical result is insufficient. The lower cis crossing point may be incorporated but need not be the sole cause. Without a valid rate/kinetic model, do not directly equate the energy difference with precise selectivity or a room-temperature isomerization rate, or treat the 99% isolated yield as dr. Thermal experiments on other products 22/27 are not direct kinetic evidence for this product.

C–C addition from the alkene to the carbonyl forms a bicyclic intermediate
C–C cleavage of the original ring yields a ring-expanded open-shell skeleton
